races.name: CopyBet BOG Today For Tomorrow's Racing Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner with solid recent form on good ground (3/21f, 4/20f), racing from a prominent style naturally but likely to lead here with no challenger — has run well at this distance and on this surface, though connections must be respected even if the horse's style_fit tag tempers confidence it will hold on under pressure.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, but he's been competitive throughout, with a third last time out 20 days back the pick of that sequence. Rated clear of these rivals and already proven over today's distance, he looks the one to beat here, with only his continued search for a win the mild reservation.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton combine in fine 14-day form (3/21), and this six-year-old has won twice and placed four times in his last five on similar going — a natural hold-up horse whose profile sits perfectly within the expected race shape, and the 4-day turnaround for connections this productive is a notable positive angle.|
runners_data.comment: Won two of his last five starts in a rock-solid sequence, rarely finishing outside the frame, and returns quickly just 4 days after his latest run. He does hold form over today's distance too, but our rating places him below the head of this field, raising doubt he can repeat that against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's runner carries the tongue-tie and visor and has shown good placed form at this trip on good ground, though his natural front-running tendency has been pushed back to midfield by the number of prominent types in this field — the style mismatch is a genuine handicap, and his trainer is 0/8 in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, but a second and a third feature among those finishes, showing he's competitive enough to trouble this field. Race-fit 15 days on and already proven over today's distance, the concern is the inconsistency either side of those placings, including one occasion he failed to complete.

runners_data.name: Suttons Hill
runners_data.note: The amateur conditional Joe Anderson (3lb claim) takes the mount for Fergal Brennan (0/1 in 14 days), and recent form reads poorly with a pulled-up and a fifth; a genuine prominent runner who will struggle to claim his natural berth close to the pace given the competition for that position, adding further doubt to an already unconvincing profile.|
runners_data.comment: A modest run of finishes masks solid ability - our rating of 105 places him among the leaders of this field, despite two non-completions in his last five starts. He was runner-up four starts back and returns 18 days on, already proven over today's distance, though that inconsistency remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Atlanta Brave
runners_data.note: Kerry Lee's eight-year-old has been placed at 25f on good ground and is a confirmed hold-up horse wearing a hood, giving him the right profile for this race shape — 40 days since last run is a mild freshness watch, but his recent five-run sequence shows consistent placed form at marathon trips with no obvious going concern.|
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence of finishes - including a ninth and two fifths in his last five starts - belies real quality, with our rating placing him second-highest in this field. He was an eye-catching third three starts back, and despite a 40-day break, that gap between bare form and figure marks him out as a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Posted
runners_data.note: Matt Sheppard's nine-year-old has a frank finishing tendency to fade when the race gets serious — flagged explicitly in the data — and his recent form shows multiple pulled-up and eighth-or-worse finishes over shorter; as a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field density, he faces both a positional and a stamina-resolution problem in the closing stages.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, with three of those runs ending in a pulled-up effort and a below-par sixth last time out, 53 days ago. Rated the field's outsider on our figures too, this is a tough sequence to find much positive in, beyond the fact he's freshened up with a break.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish. Thickthorn Tom and Atlanta Brave are the true hold-up horses in this field, likely to be held up off the pace and asked for their effort from the third-last onwards. Suttons Hill, Atreides, and Keep Me Posted are all natural prominent types, but with three horses sharing that profile and only one slot readily available behind the leader, at least two of them will be shuffled into a midfield position that does not suit them — Suttons Hill, with the lightest trainer form, is most likely to concede that battle, while Atreides may manage to settle just off the pace. The resulting race shape — a controlled single pace-setter, a compressed midfield of horses racing out of role, and genuine closers stalking at the rear — decisively favours hold-up types who can travel sweetly and produce one clean run from the home turn, making Thickthorn Tom's profile the most architecturally suited to how this race will unfold.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, closers finish
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the field strings out, allowing hold-up horses to deliver their finishing effort cleanly.
scenarios.body: Thank You Blue dictates every yard without pressure, setting a rhythm that is sustainable but still tests stamina through the final mile; hold-up horses travelling behind find daylight from the third-last and sweep through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, leader wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes so slow in the middle stages that the field concertinas and Thank You Blue pings the last with a big enough advantage to hold on.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race denies the closers the sustained gallop they need to reel in the leader, and any late kick from the chasing pack arrives too little too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent types battle it out
scenarios.trigger: If Suttons Hill or Atreides manage to race close to Thank You Blue and grind the leader into submission through a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens earlier than expected as prominently-running types jostle for position, turning the race into an extended stamina test that rewards the strongest finisher over this 2m4f trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers swamp a fading field
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners and prominent types collectively set too strong a gallop and capitulate before the last, leaving the race open to late finishers.
scenarios.body: A messy, overheated pace burns off the principals and the hold-up horses storm home from the rear, though Keep Me Posted's known tendency to fade in the finish limits its claims even in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Thickthorn Tom's 4-day turnaround with Harry Skelton and a trainer firing at 3/21 in the past fortnight makes him the standout tactical fit — watch how quickly he travels into contention approaching the third-last.

Atreides and Suttons Hill are both natural front-runners who will compete for the same limited space behind Thank You Blue — if they jostle early, it risks burning energy and compromising both their chances significantly.
Keep Me Posted's recorded tendency to fade in the finish is a live danger even if the race sets up perfectly for closers — watch whether he can maintain his effort from the second-last to the line.
Thank You Blue's uncontested lead is the fulcrum of this entire race shape — if anything causes the leader to be pressured or checked at a fence, the entire tactical picture resets dramatically.|

races.name: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: I'm A Starman
runners_data.note: Veteran 13-year-old trained by Mark Rimell, returning after 55 days off with Sean Bowen aboard; Good-ground record of 10 wins/places from 15 runs is solid and the confirmed lead role suits, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is tagged as prominent rather than pure leader — at OR 100, top weight, and this age, stamina late in the race is the key question.
runners_data.comment: I'm A Starman rounded off his recent form with a solid second, already proven over today's trip, and rates clear of this field on our figures. Fitness after 55 days off is the only slight concern for the leading fancy.

runners_data.name: Knightsbridge
runners_data.note: Six-year-old in sharp form with back-to-back wins at 20f and 24f on Good ground, and trainer Jonjo O'Neill operating at 4/14 over 14 days; a genuine hold-up type whose 10/10 Good-ground record gives enormous confidence in conditions, and the step back up to 2m7f stretches him but recent course win at 24f suggests stamina is there.
runners_data.comment: Knightsbridge arrives on the back of successive wins, a big turnaround from three below-par efforts before that spell. He's fresh from 15 days off and has today's trip covered, though our rating sees him with less in hand than his official mark suggests.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling seven-year-old with an excellent Good-ground profile (7/10) and two wins from five at 24f on similar surface; T Ellis sends out a runner 11 days after a run (1/3 in that window), tongue-tie fitted, and from a handy position just off I'm A Starman this horse is well placed to pounce if the leader weakens.
runners_data.comment: Huckleberry Sting won last time out, having also won four starts back, with a third and a second in between - arguably the most in-form runner here. Quick to back up within 11 days with today's trip covered, but he'll need to confirm that upward curve again.

runners_data.name: Carpe Diem
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose form reads 232-22 — never wins but rarely far away; Tom Hutsby (7lb claimer) is a concern at this level, 43 days off, and Good-ground record is adequate at 9/15 with no wins; at OR 91, this David Bridgwater runner is a classic place-threat rather than a likely winner.
runners_data.comment: Carpe Diem has been freakishly consistent, finishing runner-up in four of his last five starts and never worse than third, though still yet to get his head in front. He resumes after a 43-day break with today's trip covered, a threat if that near-miss run finally clicks.

runners_data.name: School For Scandal
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran at OR 80, 68 days absent, with two pulled-up runs in recent form (P and P visible); Good-ground figures of 7/15 are moderate, and without headgear noted, the trainer's 2/13 in 14 days is a minor positive, but age and spotty recent form make this a speculative each-way proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: School For Scandal pulled up last time out, having managed a third one start back after also pulling up two starts back, with a fifth and fourth further back. He has today's trip covered, but the 68-day gap and patchy sequence leave plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Henry Box Brown
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner by inclination whose Ellis Collier (5lb claim) partnership hasn't fired recently (form 446-U6); trainer Mrs C Williams at 0/6 in 14 days is a negative flag, and while Good ground is familiar (11/15), being forced into a midfield berth away from his natural position significantly reduces his effectiveness — expect him to race with some frustration rather than fluency.
runners_data.comment: Henry Box Brown followed a pair of fourths with two sixths either side of an unseated exit, without ever threatening the front rank. Our rating nudges him above his official mark, and a swift 20-day turnaround keeps him squarely in this mix.

runners_data.name: Stay Hopeful
runners_data.note: Young six-year-old at OR 74 whose form figures (99-467) tell a bleak recent story; a true hold-up runner mapped to midfield because rear positions were oversubscribed, so Henry Oliver's charge will race in an unfamiliar role — the 40-day absence and visor headgear are additional unknowns, and the Good-ground profile (3/6) is thin.
runners_data.comment: Stay Hopeful sits bottom of our rankings, his last five runs yielding no better than a fourth and including a pair of well-beaten ninths. He returns after 40 days off, but there's little in the recent form to inspire much confidence.

runners_data.name: Elfride
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old at the bottom of the weights, 90 days off which is the longest layoff in the field; Richard Phillips sends this one out at 0/7 in 14 days, and form P69P5 includes two non-completions — a genuine hold-up type who has been pushed into a mapped midfield position it won't naturally occupy, making it hard to see a winning run materialising here.
runners_data.comment: Elfride's recent form includes two exits and a well-beaten ninth, with a fifth her best effort in that time. A 90-day absence compounds the task, though she has at least covered today's trip before, for what small comfort that offers.

races.paceDynamic: I'm A Starman is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to push them hard, Sean Bowen can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m7f trip at Worcester. Huckleberry Sting and School For Scandal carry prominent styles and will track closely, but neither figures to pressure I'm A Starman for the lead from the front — they will simply slot in behind. The field holds more prominent types than can all hold their natural position: Henry Box Brown is a genuine front-runner who will be shuffled into a less comfortable midfield role, reducing their effectiveness. With a single horse dictating a measured pace over an extended chase trip on Good turf, this race shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can travel comfortably in behind and deliver a single sustained late run — but only those genuinely bred for that role, not those redistributed there by default.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If I'm A Starman sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and hold-up horses with genuine finishing ability can close in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: I'm A Starman bowls along in front at a pace that suits himself, meaning the race is run on even terms until the home straight where genuine hold-up runners Knightsbridge and Carpe Diem are best placed to deliver a clean challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If I'm A Starman is allowed to set a truly frugal gallop and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap when asked.
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen controls every yard, the pursuit never properly organises, and the 13-year-old's class and fitness on Good ground carries him all the way to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If I'm A Starman weakens late and a prominent tracker like Huckleberry Sting has stalked close enough to inherit the lead.
scenarios.body: Huckleberry Sting, with strong Good-ground form at 24f and a recent win, is ideally placed to capitalise if the pace collapses in the final two fences; School For Scandal also benefits from a prominent position if this shape emerges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough early to stretch the field but the redistributed midfield horses cannot reproduce their true running style from an unnatural position.
scenarios.body: Stay Hopeful and Elfride, both genuine hold-up types racing out of role in mapped midfield, are unlikely to produce their best; Henry Box Brown, a natural front-runner shuffled back, also underperforms, leaving the spoils to established closers with authentic tactical flexibility.

watchPoints.text: Knightsbridge is the one to track: back-to-back wins, 10/10 Good-ground record, and a genuine hold-up style that perfectly suits an uncontested lead scenario — if he travels sweetly behind I'm A Starman, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

I'm A Starman's age (13) and weight (168lbs) mean watch carefully for any signs of fatigue after the last fence — if he has run his race by then, the race could open up dramatically for a prominent tracker.

Henry Box Brown is a natural front-runner who will be racing against his instincts from midfield; watch his behaviour in the early stages as frustration or a misplaced surge to recover position could unsettle his race and take others with him.

Huckleberry Sting's trainer has a 1/3 strike rate in the 14-day window and the horse is 11 days off a run — monitor market moves as fresh money here would confirm this one is sharper than the form string suggests.

Elfride's 90-day absence is the longest in the field and the horse has two non-completions in recent form — watch the pre-race show carefully as any signs of reluctance or below-par condition could signal an early exit.

races.name: Copybet Support Safer Gambling Maiden Hurdle Race (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jorah d'Alma
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Fergal O'Brien (2/13 trainer 14-day) who handles good ground well and has placed at this trip and beyond; only 15 days since last run is not a concern and the tongue-tie is a familiar aid, but a low win-rate in recent form (0W2P in similar going) suggests a place contender rather than a winner.

runners_data.name: Mr Rafiki
runners_data.note: A consistent fourth-place finisher across his last four starts, this is a true hold-up horse whose four-from-four tendency to finish in midfield to rear means he needs a strong gallop that is unlikely to materialise here; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is an able partner but the style-fit penalty and natural race position being compromised work against him.

runners_data.name: Trigger The Light
runners_data.note: Style unclassified (U) and handles good ground, posting two placed efforts at 2m4f and 2m7f in similar conditions; Sara Bradstock's charge is 37 days off a run and the 7lb claiming rider Miss Lily Bradstock adds intrigue, but a stronger pace than Mirabello provides would suit this horse's off-the-pace profile.

runners_data.name: Loman Lady
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton's mount for Dan Skelton (3/21 trainer 14-day) won at 2m on good ground last time and has a smart strike-rate in similar conditions (1W1P); carries just 151lbs and races prominently, making her the most dangerous challenger to Mirabello if she can track the pace comfortably and produce a clean round of jumping.

runners_data.name: Mirabello
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will control the gallop unopposed, but the style-fit tag (0.93) signals she is not operating entirely within role; Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim is useful on a horse whose form shows placed efforts without winning, and at 2m7f on good ground her stamina under a slow-to-moderate pace may become a factor.

runners_data.name: Snow Is In The Sky
runners_data.note: Off 123 days and with only two hurdle runs in soft ground, this Gary Brown-trained five-year-old has limited form evidence on good and is a natural hold-up horse who has been pushed into mapped midfield because the rear is congested; both historical starts came in softer conditions, making the going an additional unknown.

runners_data.name: Walkingtheline
runners_data.note: Ben Poste partners a horse that has won over hurdles and showed a placed effort (3rd, 2m) in its most recent similar-going run; a genuine hold-up horse with hurdle headgear (ht), 15 days since last run is fine, and at 2m7f this trip extension may suit if the pace quickens sufficiently to set up a late run.

runners_data.name: Witheros Hill
runners_data.note: Back from a 459-day absence under Kevin Brogan for Laura Horsfall, this horse carries a flag warning for fading in the finish and has only one run at this distance in good ground (finished 12th); the layoff is the dominant concern and the form string (23P03/) shows a horse that has drifted in and out of competitiveness.

races.paceDynamic: Mirabello is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, she should be able to dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over this testing 2m7f trip at Worcester. Snow Is In The Sky and Mr Rafiki are both natural hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is over-subscribed — neither is likely to feature prominently in the early stages, and their redistribution further reinforces that the pace will be set by Mirabello alone without serious pressure. Loman Lady and Jorah d'Alma are legitimate prominent types who will track Mirabello and apply passive pressure, but nothing in this field is likely to force a truly searching early tempo. The race shape strongly favours a prominent or close-tracking runner who can stalk the unhurried gallop and produce a well-timed challenge from second or third, rather than a true deep closer who needs a fast-run race to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mirabello Controls; Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mirabello leads at a controlled pace and the race is set up for a prominent tracker to pounce from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Mirabello rolls along unchallenged, setting a sustainable tempo that keeps back-markers anchored and allows the prominent runners to travel well into contention; as the field strings out over the final two flights, those racing just off the pace have first run on the tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mirabello Pins Them Back; Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace is slow enough that Mirabello conserves energy and her rivals find themselves flat-footed when she kicks clear.
scenarios.body: A near-crawl through the early stages means the gallop lacks intensity and Mirabello, never headed, simply extends her lead jumping the final hurdle before rivals can close the gap; a horse carrying low weight and racing off an honest mark would be best placed to capitalise if Mirabello ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens; Midfield Sweepers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Loman Lady or Jorah d'Alma push the tempo in the back straight, creating a genuinely run race that favours horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A contested mid-race gallop opens up ground for Walkingtheline or Trigger The Light to reel in the pace from their off-the-pace positions as front-runners empty; this scenario requires the pace to be strong enough to compromise the leaders' jumping, which is possible but against the weight of evidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong in the back half of the race and the hold-up horses manage to secure their natural position and produce a late run.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because Snow Is In The Sky and Mr Rafiki, the genuine hold-up types, are displaced from their preferred rear berths and are unlikely to produce a true late flourish; Walkingtheline, the most credible closer with legitimate form, is the best candidate if the race somehow develops into a truly searing test of stamina.

watchPoints.text: Loman Lady — Harry Skelton will look to track Mirabello closely from the outset; if she travels well into the home straight she is the most likely beneficiary of the controlled pace and the one most capable of picking off the leader between the final two hurdles.

Mirabello — as sole front-runner she controls the tempo but the style-fit discount and no previous win on this profile means she may surrender the advantage if a prominent rival challenges at the third-last; watch for Isabelle Ryder keeping the gallop deceptively slow to preserve stamina.

Walkingtheline — if the pace quickens in the back straight this hold-up horse is best placed to produce a late run, but Ben Poste must find a clear passage as the field converges on the home turn; the trip extension to 2m7f is an untested factor worth monitoring.

Snow Is In The Sky — 123 days off and both career starts on soft ground make this the biggest unknown in the field; watch early in the race to see whether McLernon attempts to slot in closer than the horse's natural hold-up style to compensate for the redistributed position.

Witheros Hill — the 459-day layoff and the noted tendency to fade in the finish mean Kevin Brogan may be purely focused on getting the horse round safely; if it sets a target early before weakening, it could distort the pace picture for a brief period approaching the mid-point of the race.

races.name: CopyBet Daily Profit Boost Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Chemistry
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partnership in good recent nick; won over 17f on good ground and finished second over 16f on good, giving strong trip/going confidence, though wearing a hood and genuinely preferring to race off the pace — likely to be committed forward of its natural position given the jockey's positive approach.

runners_data.name: Square d'Alboni
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton on board is the standout jockey booking and the horse's last run — a win over 18f on good — is directly relevant; inclined to race further back than Skelton will allow, meaning the partnership may secure a prominent midfield slot that flatters its tactical position.

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over 16-18f on good ground but without a win in recent outings; Stan Sheppard is a competent claimer and the horse's stamina is not in doubt, though it has struggled to dominate and will again be racing in a position closer to midfield than it naturally prefers.

runners_data.name: Scoro
runners_data.note: Style undefined and lightly raced, which is a double flag; two runs on good over 16f produced a 6th and a 4th, so its jumping and consistency under pressure are unproven — if it does stride into the lead, it becomes a pace-setter by default rather than by design.

runners_data.name: Wait At The Gate
runners_data.note: Going marked UNKNOWN and 53 days since last run are both flags; form shows a string including a win (1) but also a pulled-up, and the combination of freshness, unknown going suitability and undefined style makes it genuinely unpredictable — capable of going forward or dropping away.

runners_data.name: Imperial Trooper
runners_data.note: Five runs across various trips suggest moderate progression at best; Jennie Candlish has runners in form (3/20 in 14 days) but this horse's best placing over comparable trips is a 3rd on good ground and it lacks the profile to quicken sharply in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Lamlash
runners_data.note: Callum Pritchard on a young horse for Joe Tickle who has two wins from 13 in 14 days — not without a trainer angle; but the recent form is a pulled-up and a dash, and two runs in similar going produced only an 8th and a 5th, giving little confidence this horse can land a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Baileys Big Image
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — a serious concern in a race expected to end in a sprint; three runs on good including a 3rd suggest it can be placed but the fade tag means the sharp finish at Worcester is likely to find it out, and it was nudged into midfield from its natural rear position.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice hurdle over 2m at Worcester, the early gallop is likely to be pedestrian, with the field coasting through the early exchanges before the tempo lifts in the home straight and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the final hurdle. Scoro and Wait At The Gate carry undefined styles and could push forward from the gate, but neither has the profile of a genuine pace-setter capable of stretching the field. Chemistry, Square d'Alboni, Connemara Joe and Baileys Big Image are all natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map because the field is simply too heavy with closers to accommodate them at the rear — of those, Square d'Alboni (Harry Skelton) and Chemistry (Sean Quinlan) are the most likely to press further forward than their natural inclination, given both jockeys' tendency to be positive. With the gallop expected to be modest and the finish compressed, horses who can travel fluently in mid-division and sustain a run through the final two hurdles are best placed — a race shape that rewards those with tactical speed and sound jumping, rather than pure late closers who need a true pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Mid-Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the race unfolds at an honest-but-not-brutal gallop and the field bunches heading to the last, rewarding horses who travel well and quicken off modest fractions.
scenarios.body: The compressed finish suits runners positioned prominently enough to exploit the final sprint without needing a true pace to bring them into the race; sound jumping and tactical pace off the final bend become the deciding factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow early and the pace only picks up sharply from three out, giving genuine hold-up horses a late run that arrives in time.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling early tempo can paradoxically help horses who travel smoothly at the rear and quicken — provided the last-flight jumping is clean; Imperial Trooper and Lamlash, with their modest records, are unlikely beneficiaries but the profile suits the cleaner hold-up operators.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Fittest Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Scoro or Wait At The Gate presses forward and sets a genuine gallop that strings the field out, creating a test of stamina and fitness over staying power.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace over 2m at Worcester on good ground would filter out the lighter-raced runners — Connemara Joe, whose recent form shows repeated placed efforts over comparable trips in similar going, could stay on best from mid-division if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Jumping Errors Decisive
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners make jumping errors or falter at crucial hurdles under a bunched, hectic finish, leaving the race to whoever clears the final flight cleanly.
scenarios.body: Poor-jumping incidents in compressed novice fields can dramatically shuffle the finish order regardless of running style; any runner who meets the last on a good stride and travels fluently through the melee benefits disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Baileys Big Image is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — in a race almost certain to be decided by a sprint from the final hurdle, monitor whether it can sustain its effort or drops away under pressure, which could cause interference if it stops sharply in a bunched field.

Wait At The Gate returns after 53 days, has unknown going suitability and an undefined running style — watch how it settles and whether it attempts to take an early lead, as that would fundamentally alter the pace dynamic and drag other hold-up types into a different race shape.

Harry Skelton on Square d'Alboni may attempt to push forward from the natural hold-up position — if the Skelton/Skelton combination secures a prominent spot early, it becomes a major tactical threat that the map positioning currently understates.

With Scoro and Wait At The Gate both carrying undefined styles and genuine uncertainty about the going, watch the early stages closely — if neither commits to the front, the field could crawl to the halfway point, compressing the finish to the point where jumping quality at the last becomes the only differentiator.

races.name: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: David Pipe's in-form yard (2/10 in 14 days) sends a 5-year-old who improved sharply last autumn, winning over 2m6f on Good and placing twice more at similar trips — Jack Tudor retains the ride and the tongue-tie/visor combo has coincided with his best form; a true hold-up type with strong evidence for this trip and going.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, having previously run a third, a fourth and a sixth - a solid recent profile. Fit again 23 days on and with proven form over today's distance, that rounded profile makes him our narrow selection, with just a shade of dip earlier in the sequence to note.

runners_data.name: The Great Escape
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes over for a horse whose six placings in recent starts suggest consistent effort without the winning sharpness; his best form has come at 2m-2m6f on Good and the step to 2m7f is a question, though 55 days off and a yard in decent recent flow (4/14) make him one of the more reliable hold-up finishers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Well below his best in recent starts — a pair of eighths, a seventh, and a pulled-up effort each feature in his last five, with a below-par sixth last time out — yet our rating of 99 makes him the clear leader of this field on ability alone. Fresh for this after a 55-day break, that recent losing sequence remains the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Longsdon's lightly-campaigned 6-year-old ran just 12 days ago and carries the burden of a 0/3 trainer 14-day record; a natural hold-up horse whose style fit is compromised here (STYLE_FIT 0.91) because the glut of rear-pacers pushes him into a midfield role that is not his preference, and his form string (5533P) points to a horse in modest form.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five outings, but a pair of thirds and a pair of fifths show a fair level of ability, matched by our rating placing him third-best in this field. Race-fit 12 days on from his latest start, the concern is that run ended with him pulled up, the outlier in an otherwise solid sequence.

runners_data.name: Kantagua Du Large
runners_data.note: Clive Boultbee-Brooks fields a tongue-plate runner whose best two runs — 4th twice on Good — came at shorter trips (2m2f, 2m4f), and at 2m7f on Good he is stepping into uncertain territory; nudged into a midfield slot on the map though naturally a hold-up type, his STYLE_FIT of 0.90 flags that the race shape does not play to his strengths and his 0/11 record on Good going is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, and the form has faded gradually — two fourths, then two sixths, before a below-par ninth last time. She has proven form over today's distance and returns 18 days on, but that softening sequence is the clear concern despite a competitive rating.

runners_data.name: Hardy Buck
runners_data.note: Max Comley's 8-year-old returns from 155 days off — a flag for fitness — and Luke Scott claims 3lb, but his sole Good-ground win came at 2m3f and his recent figures on similar going (9/15 sim-going) are modest; his hood has been tried before and though he won on Soft at 2m3f, the lack of recent racecourse evidence makes him a speculative each-way hope rather than a confident selection.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out, his second such non-completion in this sequence, with a modest seventh and an earlier win also in the book. He was runner-up one start back and holds form over today's distance, so the ability is there, but a 155-day absence and that mixed record make him hard to trust fresh.

runners_data.name: Fane Court
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy partners an 8-year-old who ran just 6 days ago — very quick back — and whose best placing in this data (3rd, 2m3f, Good) gives a credible platform for this trip; D J Jeffreys's yard has had 0/4 in 14 days and the horse's style is hold-up at heart, redistributed to midfield on the map, but his form figures (43 latest) suggest he is in a reasonable vein and handles Good well.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, though a third last time out just 6 days ago is the form to take heart from. Two fourths and a pulled-up effort further back in that sequence show why he's up against it here, and while he does hold form over today's distance, this looks a stiff task on pure figures.

runners_data.name: Warner's Cross
runners_data.note: Sophie Leech's 9-year-old has 1W4P on similar going and a strong 10/15 sim-going record, but six months off (66 days since last run), an OR of 75, and five consecutive placed-or-worse finishes without a win temper enthusiasm; Sean Bowen's presence lifts the horse's prospects of getting a clear run, and his natural tendency to race deeply held (redistributed here) means he needs things to fall right late in the day.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts and three finishes down the field, yet our rating of 89 sits well above his official mark of 75, hinting at unexploited ability. A 66-day absence raises a fitness question, leaving him more an each-way watch than a confident vote.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of seven genuine hold-up horses with no confirmed front-runner, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and contested by whichever runner is pushed forward reluctantly — almost certainly producing a crawl through the first mile before the tempo lifts sharply in the latter stages. With Final Entry, The Great Escape, Ikigai Star, Kantagua Du Large, Hardy Buck, Fane Court, and Warner's Cross all preferring to race off the pace, there is no natural pace-setter to string the field out, and the race shape will default to a bunched, slow-run affair that explodes into a stamina-testing sprint finish over the final two hurdles. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Ikigai Star, Kantagua Du Large, Hardy Buck, Fane Court, and Warner's Cross are all redistributed in the map, and whichever rider is pushed widest or finds themselves unable to get cover may be forced to take up a more prominent role involuntarily, with Final Entry (Jack Tudor, David Pipe) and The Great Escape (Jonjo O'Neill Jr.) best positioned by class and jockey profile to capitalise. This race shape strongly favours horses with a high cruising speed in the closing stages, a proven ability to accelerate off a slow pace, and a jockey capable of positioning for one run — class hold-up types with good recent form on Good ground hold the tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the early stages and the race degenerates into a sprint off the home turn, as the absence of a front-runner strongly suggests.
scenarios.body: The tempo will be minimal until the field rounds into the straight, at which point position and acceleration matter above stamina; horses with the best turn of foot and an agile jumper profile will dominate. Final Entry's improved 2024 form over 2m6f-3m on Good ground and Jack Tudor's positional awareness make this shape ideal, while The Great Escape's prior experience at this sort of trip adds each-way substance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up earlier than expected from the second circuit and a genuine gallop develops, rewarding horses who travel smoothly and finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: A more genuine tempo would spread the field and expose horses who struggle to sustain effort over 2m7f, suiting those who settle, travel kindly, and produce a measured late run rather than a flat-out sprint. Fane Court's consistent placing record at this distance on Good ground and Tom Bellamy's tactical nous make this shape worth monitoring, while Final Entry's stamina credentials and David Pipe's strong recent 14-day record give him additional substance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of a natural leader causes positional confusion, bunching at hurdles, and interference that scrambles the finish and opens the door for a lower-rated runner.
scenarios.body: In a race where every horse wants to race in the same position, erratic early movement and jumping errors become genuinely disruptive, and a hold-up horse that finds clear daylight soonest through the melee can win despite modest form figures. Hardy Buck (OR 81) has shown ability at this sort of trip when fresh conditions suit and Luke Scott claims 3lb, while Warner's Cross's consistency at 2m4f-3m on Good ground for Sophie Leech gives a plausible upset angle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Forced Winner
scenarios.trigger: If one horse is pushed into an uncontested lead by circumstance and dictates a steady, confidence-boosting gallop that suits a relaxed front-running style nobody anticipated.
scenarios.body: In a field of reluctant leaders, the horse coerced forward earliest could secure an uncontested lead and control all the fractions, effectively stealing the race by dictating a pace that keeps rivals' engines ticking over while their own settles well. Kantagua Du Large or Ikigai Star — each redistributed but with some early pace in their histories — could find themselves up front and difficult to peg back if connections choose not to fight for position.

watchPoints.text: Final Entry and The Great Escape are the two highest-rated hold-up horses in a field with no true front-runner — if either secures the best position off the home turn, they become very difficult to pass in a sprint finish and should be monitored from two out.

Hardy Buck has been off 155 days and returns cold — watch his jumping early, as a horse returning from a lengthy break in a slow-run race over hurdles can make costly errors if not fully tuned, which could compromise every runner he involves in.

With five genuine hold-up types redistibuted into midfield on the map (Ikigai Star, Kantagua Du Large, Hardy Buck, Fane Court, Warner's Cross), watch the early part of the race for a chaotic, bunched field — interference at the first two hurdles is a genuine risk given the clustering of similar-styled horses.

Fane Court ran just six days ago — watch whether Tom Bellamy elects to take a more prominent role given the absence of a genuine front-runner, as a horse this fresh in a slow-run race could benefit from forcing the tempo rather than waiting for others.

runners_data.name: Prince Imperial
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner dropping back in distance who goes well on good ground (sim-going strike rate solid), though a nine-year-old with a run of placed efforts and a 55-day break; wears a tongue-tie and visor — needs to jump cleanly to exploit his positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Prince Imperial sits top of our ratings for this nine-runner field, with today's trip already proven. His recent starts have been underwhelming, but a fully fit effort following 55 days off makes him the one to beat on pure class.

runners_data.name: October Hill
runners_data.note: David Pipe in 2/10 form over the last fortnight with this six-year-old who won last time out over 2m on soft, now stepping up to 2m4f on good — the longer trip is a genuine query but good-ground runs at 2m show talent and Rian Corcoran (5lb) is a positive claim.
runners_data.comment: October Hill was brought down last time, having won one start back after a third and a second. A competitive rating and the trip covered work in her favour, though an eighth further back shows there's a ceiling.

runners_data.name: Shesonnet
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with an excellent good-ground profile — three of her five runs on similar ground produced top-two finishes including a win — and Ben Case's yard has a runner declared; the step to 2m4f from 2m1f last time looks workable for a five-year-old mare still progressing.
runners_data.comment: Shesonnet was second last time out, having won three starts back, though an eighth in between and a pulled-up effort further out point to some inconsistency. She matches this field on rating and has the trip covered, but needs her better side to show.

runners_data.name: Leave Her To Me
runners_data.note: Long absence (216 days) is the obvious concern for a mare who has won twice on good ground over today's trip, but she won fresh before and the McPherson/Killahena yard had a winner recently; her hold-up style needs the pace to be genuine, which is not guaranteed here.
runners_data.comment: Leave Her To Me won four starts back but has since faded through a fifth, a ninth and a pulled-up run. She's proven over today's trip and rated competitively enough to feature, though a lengthy 216-day absence is the obvious concern for this comeback.

runners_data.name: Golden Glance
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor rides a horse who has won on good ground over 2m and finished fourth last time after a string of midfield efforts; the hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong in front, but his recent consistency in similar company keeps him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Golden Glance won one start back and followed with a fair fourth last time, having managed nothing better than a seventh in the three runs before that. Fresh from 20 days off with today's trip covered, our rating sees her as a leading improver - though inconsistency remains the risk.

runners_data.name: Phantom Gold
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan takes over a prominent racer whose entire recent form history was compiled on good ground — six runs, all on good, including a win and three placed efforts; the step up to 2m4f from his last few runs at 2m is the main question.
runners_data.comment: Phantom Gold has been runner-up in each of his last two starts, continuing a solid sequence, and our rating rates him well above his official mark. Yet to convert those efforts into a win, a rapid 15-day turnaround keeps him fresh for another bold bid.

runners_data.name: Dublinofficecallin
runners_data.note: Kerry Lee's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse by inclination, though the redistribution flag reflects the crowded rear of this field — his one win came on good ground over 2m and he has struggled on soft, so conditions suit; style-fit discount applies because clean passage from the back is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Dublinofficecallin won three starts back, a mixed recent picture since with a seventh and an unplaced effort. He does have today's trip covered and our rating flags a shade of untapped potential above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who has placed consistently on good ground but has yet to win over this trip, and whose natural rear-of-field style is squeezed by the number of genuine closers in the race — the redistribution to midfield reflects the race shape rather than his instinct, and his 0W record in 15 sim-going runs tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Royal Rhythm has pulled up twice in his last five starts and never finished better than fifth, a tough profile to trust. He is at least fresh from a run just 9 days ago and has today's trip covered, for what encouragement that provides.

runners_data.name: Locked Down Lad
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's six-year-old has a modest form profile — best effort a sixth on good ground over 2m — and the prominent style has not yet translated into a win; 15 days since last run is fine, but he faces stiffer tasks at OR 83 in this company.
runners_data.comment: Locked Down Lad sits bottom of our rankings, with the last five starts yielding no better than sixth and including a pulled-up run and an unseated exit. Today's trip is at least covered, but the recent evidence stacks up firmly against him.

races.paceDynamic: Prince Imperial is the lone confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press him from the off, he should control the tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable pace over 2m4f on good ground. Phantom Gold and October Hill are both prominent types who will want to sit just behind him, creating a compact early order but without the friction that generates a truly searching gallop. With Dublinofficecallin and Royal Rhythm both natural hold-up horses redistributed to the midfield map position — because the field contains more rear-runners than the race shape can physically accommodate — the closers' end of the race may be more crowded and less clean than it appears on paper. This shape — a controlled pace with a small lead group and a compressed midfield — suits patient prominent racers who travel well and can challenge from the second-last hurdle, rather than true hold-up horses needing a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Imperial sets a sustainable gallop and the race is run at a steady-to-fair pace with no serious challenger for the lead.
scenarios.body: Prince Imperial dictates on his own terms and the horses tracking him in the prominent group — particularly October Hill and Phantom Gold — get an ideal rhythm before asserting after the second-last hurdle; this shape is tailor-made for horses who travel close to the pace and can respond on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely honest enough to string the field out and leave a gap for a strong finisher to come through.
scenarios.body: Shesonnet or Leave Her To Me, both genuine hold-up types with solid good-ground form, would find more late petrol than the leaders if fatigue sets in over the final climb; this scenario requires a more searching gallop than the pace map suggests is likely, making it a secondary outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that Prince Imperial or one of the prominent horses idles into the final stretch and simply outstays the field.
scenarios.body: A very dawdling tempo would see the field bunch entering the straight with no momentum to run through, handing the initiative to whoever has been in front all along; Prince Imperial's jumping and front-running experience gives him the edge if the race becomes a sprint from the last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If scrimmaging in the pack disrupts the fancied hold-up types and an underestimated runner finds daylight at the right moment.
scenarios.body: With Dublinofficecallin and Royal Rhythm both racing out of their natural positions and potentially interfering with each other's run, a lower-rated runner like Golden Glance — recent winner, good-ground specialist — could benefit from a gap appearing; this is a low-probability chaotic scenario relying on things going wrong for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Prince Imperial has not run for 55 days and wears a tongue-tie — if he jumps poorly early or gets tired in the closing stages after controlling the fractions, the race opens up dramatically for the prominent trackers.

Leave Her To Me returns from 216 days off; watch how sharply she moves in the parade ring and early in the race — if she looks light or sluggish she is unlikely to get competitive despite strong good-ground form over today's trip.

Dublinofficecallin and Royal Rhythm are both natural hold-up horses potentially taking up similar positions in a compressed midfield — traffic interference between them in the back straight is a credible risk that could compromise both runners simultaneously.

October Hill's jockey claim (5lb from Rian Corcoran) is significant in a competitive handicap — weigh whether the inexperience burden at 166lbs net is offset by the trip, as his best form was at 2m on soft rather than 2m4f on good.

Phantom Gold's entire recent form base is on good ground at shorter trips — if he travels sweetly in the prominent group and the pace is modest, his jumping efficiency and course-relevant experience could see him outrun his OR 98 mark.
